clue.text: Bachelor's amorous spirit

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree
randy is informal British for lustful or amorous

explanation.surface: An unmarried man is in a romantic mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled liquor, and spirit is the general word for such strong drink.

clue.text: Polish water supply is hot

parts.note: a burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream, a source of water
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A Polish household's water comes out hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' poses as the nationality; it is the verb. A BURN is a small stream in Scotland and northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To burnish metal is to rub it until it shines, which is to polish it.

clue.text: The Guardian starts to assess Roman government under Severus

indicators.note: the starts of the following words, their first letters, are taken in turn

explanation.surface: This newspaper begins to evaluate how Rome was ruled under the emperor Septimius Severus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Guardian' looks like the newspaper but is the definition: Argus, the hundred-eyed watchman of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Argus Panoptes was the many-eyed giant set to watch over Io, so his name stands for a vigilant guardian.

clue.text: Deceased Dickensian resident

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died or deceased, as in genealogies
Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in The Pickwick Papers by Charles Dickens

explanation.surface: A Dickens character living somewhere has died.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is one who lives in a place, so it is a synonym for resident.

clue.text: Guardian staff promote retiring film director

parts.note: the newspaper's staff refer to themselves editorially as we

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for promote is written backwards

parts.note: to sell an idea or product is to promote it

explanation.surface: Newspaper employees publicise a reclusive moviemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' poses as shy, describing the director, but signals going backwards; a newspaper's staff write editorially in the first person plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane and is one of cinema's most famous directors.

clue.text: Anticipate old Paddy catching cold

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the word for Paddy catches, or holds inside it, the letter for cold

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper, as is a pet in the phrase in a pet
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone expects an old Irishman to come down with a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' suggests an Irishman, but here it means a temper tantrum, PET.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to look forward to it as likely, which is to anticipate it.

clue.text: The French remove clothing that's cleaner

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to undress is to take off one's clothes

explanation.surface: A French housekeeper strips off as she cleans.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman who washes clothes and linen, a kind of cleaner.

clue.text: Reckoning to eat fowl — part of the breast

indicators.note: the word for reckoning eats, taking inside it, the word for fowl

parts.note: a sum is a calculation or reckoning
a tern is a seabird, loosely a fowl

explanation.surface: Settling the bill for dinner, someone eats a bit of chicken breast.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: A great dentist worked in an industrial centre

indicators.note: worked suggests material shaped or kneaded into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fine dentist practises in a factory area.
explanation.definitionFit: A trading estate is a planned area of factories and warehouses, an industrial centre.

clue.text: Democratic newspaper, commonly a nuisance

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat or Democratic in US politics
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A left-leaning tabloid is a common irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' marks the sense as colloquial: a drag is a tedious bore.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech a drag is something tiresome or annoying, a nuisance.

clue.text: Poor Rupert Dean is delighted

indicators.note: poor signals that the names are in bad shape and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rupert and Dean are hard up yet very happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Enraptured means filled with rapture, intensely delighted.

clue.text: Girl with a Latin prayer book

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A young woman studies Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book containing the prayers and texts of the Catholic Mass.

clue.text: Some years with conservation group that's corrupt

parts.note: a decade is a span of ten years
NT is the National Trust, the British charity that conserves historic buildings and land

explanation.surface: A long spell working with heritage charities proves morally rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means in moral decline, self-indulgent and corrupt.

clue.text: Guard of honour provides tea for each individual

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
per means for each, as in per person
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A ceremonial guard hands out a cup of tea to each person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard of honour' reads as a ceremonial line of soldiers; here it is someone guarding a young woman's honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies a young unmarried woman to protect her reputation, guarding her honour.

clue.text: Poor signs affected expectations of the future

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular noun: a forecast of how things will go

indicators.note: affected means acted upon and altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad omens colour people's forecasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast, especially of how an illness will develop.

clue.text: Steering gear made of hardwood?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as in pencil grades
elm is a kind of tree and its wood

explanation.surface: A ship's tiller is carved from tough timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hardwood' is read as hard plus wood: H for hard, then ELM as the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is the tiller or wheel by which a ship is steered.

clue.text: Quietly paddle in front of boat

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to paddle is to row a small boat

explanation.surface: Someone paddles softly at the head of a canoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the pointed front part of a ship's bow.

clue.text: Footballers absorbed by subject of foul

indicators.note: the footballers are taken inside the word for subject

parts.note: prone, as in prone to colds, means subject to or liable to
FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body

explanation.surface: Players are on the receiving end of a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane language is foul, coarse or blasphemous.

clue.text: Poverty-stricken journalists going into action

indicators.note: the journalists go into the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
the press is a collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters spring into action over a poverty story.
explanation.definitionFit: A depressed area or economy is one suffering hardship and low income, poverty-stricken.

clue.text: Steward takes lithium to relax

indicators.note: the word for steward takes the chemical symbol inside it

parts.note: a reeve was a steward or manager of an estate in medieval England
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A manager takes a mood-stabilising drug to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve tension or strain is to ease or relax it.

clue.text: Bird slow to reproduce

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
late, as in running late, means behind time or slow

explanation.surface: A flightless bird is too sluggish to breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduce' looks like breeding, but means copying.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to imitate or copy them, reproducing their behaviour.

clue.text: Church supports Irishman in spirit-raising

indicators.note: in a down clue the church sits below, supporting, the Irishman

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman's church backs his dabbling in the occult.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting where people try to contact or raise the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Many admit defeat when 17

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number, hence many
to own, as in own up, is to admit
to beat is to defeat

explanation.surface: A crowd concedes it has lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when 17' refers to 17 across: the answer describes someone in that state, low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat means gloomy or pessimistic, a mood of low spirits.

clue.text: Task makes sailor wear a frown

indicators.note: the sailor is worn by, so placed inside, the frown

parts.note: to lour is to frown or scowl
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A job makes a seaman scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is work or toil, so a task.

clue.text: Escort knight into custody on US ship

indicators.note: the knight goes into the word for custody

parts.note: the brig is a ship's prison, US naval slang
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is taken prisoner aboard an American warship.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone somewhere is to accompany or escort them there.

clue.text: Broken item on seat in home

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something has broken on a chair at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors, a type of home.

clue.text: One administered land

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to run an organisation is to administer it

explanation.surface: One person ran the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in western Asia, and land here means a nation.

clue.text: A tree's chopped up for festival

indicators.note: chopped up means cut into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fells a tree for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection.

clue.text: Inadequate Frenchman's a bore

parts.note: M is monsieur, the French equivalent of Mr
an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' suggests a tedious person; it is a tidal wave in a river, EAGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity or quality, inadequate.
